extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral and experienced researchers (international) applying for the Humboldt Research Fellowship; also prospective German hosts and expert reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection criteria for applying to the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation's Humboldt Research Fellowship (postdoc and experienced researcher streams) for a research stay in Germany. Covers eligibility, required documents, selection criteria, host obligations, and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic career and academic record to date
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic career and academic record to date (mobility, determination, thematic scope, academic productivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of the selection committee's core criteria; the applicant's career trajectory, mobility and productivity will be assessed relative to career stage. Consideration is individual and may take into account career breaks and equal-opportunity issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the key publications named in the application
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of the key publications named in the application (originality, innovativeness, evaluation of your own contributions to publications involving several authors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select works that particularly highlight your qualification; in multiple authorship indicate your contribution; experienced researchers should show thematic leadership. Key publications must be uploaded as unencrypted PDFs and may be 1–3 items only (at least one required). You should briefly explain the significance of each key publication and your role. Publications not yet published must have proof (acceptance letter) or be omitted per rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and innovative potential of the proposed research
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality and innovative potential of your proposed research: significance for the further development of the subject area, convincing selection of scientific methods, potential for scientific development, clear focus and feasibility within the requested sponsorship period, viability at the host institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers focus on whether the project is original (not routine), provides impetus for the field, and is feasible within the funding period and at the host. Lack of originality or a project that is a direct continuation of the doctoral thesis (without clear independent development) often leads to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Your future potential (academic potential, personal development, career prospects, e.g. professorial appointment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection considers prospects for career progression and the applicant's potential to develop into independent academic positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent research profile (experienced researchers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your independent research profile (for experienced researchers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experienced researchers must demonstrate an established, independent research profile, thematic leadership (e.g., sole/corresponding authorship), an appropriate leadership role (assistant professor/lecturer/head of independent research group or higher) and evidence of independent academic establishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality / target-group eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not a German national. Exceptions: German nationals (or those who obtained key qualifications in Germany) may apply if they have lived and worked abroad for more than ten years; with five years abroad and a strong connection to current residence (permanent employment, additional citizenship, etc.) they may also qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The programme primarily addresses researchers from abroad. Educational residents (those who completed school and university in Germany) are generally ineligible. If in doubt, applicants should contact the Foundation for advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residence / prior-stay-in-Germany rule (90 days / 18 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: For eligibility you may not have lived in Germany for longer than a total of 90 days within the 18-month period prior to submitting your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All time spent in Germany in the 18 months prior to application counts, regardless of reason. Individuals who earned their living from German institutions or worked on a doctoral project in Germany for more than 90 days in that period are ineligible. Formal eligibility is assessed on the date the Foundation receives the application. Contact the Foundation if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host confirmation and mentoring agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A researcher at a German academic institution must provide a mentoring agreement and written confirmation that research facilities are available; host must compile a detailed review and upload required documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application will only be forwarded to the Foundation once the host has uploaded all necessary documents. Hosts cannot be close personal relations (marriage/partnership, parents, siblings, children). If you have already worked in Germany for ≥12 months, the Selection Committee generally rejects returning to the same supervisor or mentor for lack of independent development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert reviews (two) and who should provide them
rubrics_metrics.description: Two expert reviews must be provided: postdocs should submit reviews from their doctoral supervisor and one other researcher (preferably outside their institute); experienced researchers should provide reviews from important collaborative partners and/or researchers at their institute and other institutes (ideally from abroad).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert reviewers upload reviews themselves in a protected area; reviews must not be more than 12 months old at time of application. The host's statement does not count as an expert review. Applicants can only submit once reviewers have uploaded their documents and the portal is open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Language requirements vary by discipline: Natural sciences and engineering: good German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: good German if necessary for research, otherwise good English suffices. Physicians: German required if research involves patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A German language certificate is required only when German knowledge is necessary (e.g., for patient work or discipline-specific needs). English or German native speakers need not submit certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to rules of good scientific practice and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: You must abide by the rules of good scientific practice and the principles of scientific ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation provides information on handling generative AI in the selection area. Misrepresentation (e.g., inaccurate publication information) can lead to formal rejection and possible sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition for previous Humboldt-sponsored applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not apply for the Humboldt Research Fellowship if you have already received sponsorship directly from the Humboldt Foundation (research fellowship or award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Former Humboldt-sponsored researchers should instead use alumni programmes; exceptions not allowed for direct repeat sponsorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document completeness and conformity to specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that fail to include important documents/information or diverge substantially from specifications (e.g., for creating a list of publications) will be formally rejected without further review; ambiguities usually postpone decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are requested to check documents carefully for completeness, accuracy and full compliance. Incomplete or inaccurate applications take longer to process and often must be postponed to a later Selection Committee meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application documents and format limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory uploads: curriculum vitae (two pages max), research outline (five pages max), complete list of publications (follow sample), list of selected key publications (follow sample), key publications (PDFs), doctoral certificate or proof of completion or confirmation that doctorate will be completed before selection meeting, German language certificate if required, publisher acceptance notifications/acknowledgements/translations if relevant, two expert reviews, detailed host statement and confirmation of research facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications must be uploaded as unencrypted PDFs. Only cite works in print, accepted, or submitted (with publisher acknowledgement); dissertations/habilitations may be cited as key publications even if not yet printed (upload manuscript). You must cite at least one key publication and may select up to three; surplus key publications will be removed without notice. You cannot amend publication lists once the review process has started.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules on which publications may be listed
rubrics_metrics.description: Only cite publications that are already in print, have been accepted for publication, or have at least been submitted to a publishing house. Cite submitted publications without naming the journal unless an acknowledgement is provided. Dissertation/habilitation may be cited as key publication if manuscript uploaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide required confirmations will result in removal of the publication from lists or formal rejection; check accuracy to avoid sanctions under Rules of Good Scientific Practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-stage limits and treatment of career breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdocs: doctorate completed during last four years (exceptions for recognised career breaks). Experienced researchers: doctorate completed during last twelve years (with possible exceptions up to 16 years in fields/countries where doctorates are uncommon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognised career breaks (child-rearing, military/alternative service, care for relatives, long-term illness, institute closures during lockdowns) may extend eligibility periods up to a limit of 6 years. Mothers can claim two extra years per child born after PhD plus verifiable parenting periods; fathers/others are credited for verifiable parenting periods. Job hunting, unemployment and non-academic employment do not count as career breaks. Applicants should declare career breaks in the application form and may contact the Foundation for advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of career paths for equal opportunities / accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection considers individual life journey and educational background and in particular equal opportunities and accessibility (e.g., barriers to mobility, gender-specific discrimination, difficult research conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to disclose personal circumstances so these can be taken into account in assessment. The Foundation's equal-opportunities statement and supports are available for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of host (who can be host and multiple hosts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any researcher at a German university or research institution offering research facilities may be host. If you have already worked in Germany for ≥12 months, you should seek a new academic environment. Hosts at different institutes may both act as hosts if each provides a host's statement and confirmation of facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosts who are close personal relations (spouse/partner, parents, siblings, children) cannot be hosts. Host institutes may receive monthly allowances for research costs (typical amounts given for natural sciences/engineering and humanities/social sciences).

rubrics_metrics.name: What frequently causes applications to be rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: Common causes for rejection: insufficient publication record (especially immediate postdoc applicants lacking published key findings), lack of academic development (project is direct continuation of doctoral thesis or returning to same supervisor/mentor), lack of originality (routine work, unclear significance), lack of personal academic profile/establishment (no/insufficient sole-authored or thematically leading publications, topics too narrow).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure key findings are published or accepted, choose projects that demonstrate independent development and originality, and show clear academic profile and thematic leadership appropriate to the programme stream.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and permissions for research stays outside Germany during the fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: Research stays outside Germany during the sponsorship period are permitted only under certain circumstances if necessary for the research (fieldwork, archives, experiments, cooperation) or for personal/organizational reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are eligible to conduct research outside Germany only if the project is carried out at the host institute in Germany for at least six months; total duration outside Germany usually should not exceed 25% of total funding period. Early or late outside stays are exceptional. Additional earnings abroad must be reported and are usually deducted from the fellowship amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration, division, start timing and language course
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdocs: fellowships may last 6–24 months (monthly €3,000 plus benefits); experienced researchers: 6–18 months (monthly €3,600 plus benefits). Fellowships may be divided into up to three stays within three years. A two- to four-month intensive German language course takes place immediately prior to the research fellowship (language fellowship is not part of the research fellowship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earliest start after approval: usually two months (three if visa required) for applicants from abroad; if already in Germany, start may be the following month. Start must be no less than two and no more than twelve months after selection meeting (language course precedes start if required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on concurrent applications to Humboldt programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot apply to several Humboldt Foundation fellowship programmes concurrently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejected by one programme you may apply to another if you meet its formal requirements. You may, however, file parallel applications to other institutions, but these must be declared on the application form and any decisions communicated to the Foundation while your application is under consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert-review process innovations (peer-circle) and review timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are evaluated by independent peer reviewers; the Foundation piloted a peer-circle process where groups of reviewers compare and discuss several applications on a protected platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical review timeline: verification 4–8 weeks, review approx. 3–6 months, selection Feb/Mar, June/July, Oct/Nov. Applicants and hosts are informed promptly after the selection meeting; grant documents provided approx. 4 weeks after selection if approved.
